Chapter 05 of 18

The Wire Choir

BroadcastEast Van / citywide100 BPM
The story

If you stand in an East Van lane and listen, you can hear it. Power lines, trolley wires, transformers, rail signals, radios, club sound systems, feedback, street hum and bass. In Terminal City these are not separate noises. They are all parts of one enormous instrument called the Wire Choir, and it is how the city talks to itself.

Terminal City does not really tell the difference between music and information. Tempo tells you how urgent something is. Bass carries weight. Repetition means the message was received. Even silence is a message. When every wire in the city goes quiet at the same moment, it means Terminal City is listening.

The crows follow the choir on their rounds. The Probes feed it news from outside, and the Far Shore translates the signals nobody understands. There is only one place it cannot reach: the Green Static of Stanley Park, where every signal fades into the trees. Hum low. Hum high. Bass carries. City knows.

Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented. Photograph reality. Alter the evidence. Never illustrate the whole myth.
